_about: Diplomacy. Every nation sits on a seven-step alignment track from Allied member to Axis member. A neutral's public opinion runs from -100 (Allies) to +100 (Axis). Each month it drifts back toward its 'home' leaning and is pushed by whoever is winning the war (momentum x bandwagon). At +/-leanAt it starts leaning (trade and treaties); at +/-joinAt it asks to join that bloc; below +/-backAt it steps back to neutrality. Players spend political capital to court neutrals; 'resist' makes some of them much harder to move. Events are history written as data: each fires once, in its window, only if its conditions still hold. Besides annex, cede, war, spawn, opinion and join, an event can 'wake' a country that has stood aside until now (it enters at the given place on the track), and 'partition' one that ends: each share is [who takes it, the regions], the first taker on the list still in the war gets whatever of those regions the country still holds, and ground someone else already holds stays theirs. Conditions include 'war:A,B' (those two are at war), 'dormant:A' and 'anyHeld:bloc,place,place' (that bloc holds at least one of the places) and 'allHeld:bloc,place,place' (it holds them all), and 'since:event:id,n' (that event happened at least n months ago). 'reform' remakes a nation's armed forces from that month on: for each nation named, the new quality of its troops, strength of its air force, whether its command is still slow, and how many corps it can put into one attack. An event with nothing but a text is a piece of news.

events.text: The Soviet Union occupies the Baltic states under the secret terms of its pact with Germany.
Moscow hands Romania an ultimatum. Bessarabia and northern Bukovina pass to the Soviet Union, and Bucharest looks to Berlin for protection.
Alarmed by the fate of the Baltic states, Finland grants German troops the right of transit.
Germany and Italy settle the Hungarian claim on Romania at Vienna. Northern Transylvania goes to Hungary.
King Carol abdicates. General Antonescu takes power in Romania and invites a German military mission.
Berlin invites the states of the Danube to sign the Tripartite Pact.
German troops gather on the Danube and Sofia is pressed to choose a side.
Officers in Belgrade overthrow the regent for leaning toward the Axis, and crowds cheer the young King. Berlin now counts Yugoslavia an enemy.
Rome follows Berlin into the war in the east and promises an Italian army for the Russian front.
Japan attacks the American fleet at Pearl Harbor, and Germany and Italy declare war on the United States. America is in the war, with the greatest industry on earth behind it.
After three days of fighting Admiral Darlan orders a ceasefire, and French North Africa comes over to the Allies. Germany and Italy occupy the rest of France, and Axis troops fly into Tunis.
The last Axis troops in Africa have laid down their arms. General Alexander signals London: "We are masters of the North African shores."

Two years of war have remade the Red Army. Its generals now handle tank armies and whole fronts in a single operation, and the factories beyond the Urals send them more tanks, guns and aircraft than Germany can build.

With Africa lost, a quarter of a million men gone into captivity at Tunis and the bombers over Sicily and Rome, the Italian army has no heart left for this war. Its divisions will not fight as they did.
The Fascist Grand Council has voted against Mussolini. The King has dismissed him and had him arrested, and Marshal Badoglio forms a government. "The war goes on," says Rome, and nobody believes it.

Italy has signed an armistice with the Allies and is out of the war. German troops disarm the Italian army, seize Rome and take over Italy's garrisons from the Riviera to Rhodes. Sardinia and Corsica are given up.
